subject: goliath frog
title: The World's Biggest Frog Moves Rocks Half Its Weight, and Scientists Finally Know Why

scenes.text: The biggest frog on Earth was caught moving rocks. Nobody knew why until 2019.
The goliath frog of Cameroon. Over 34 centimetres long without the legs, and up to 3.3 kilos. A frog the size of a house cat.
Along one river, scientists found 22 strange rock-lined pools. Some had stones of two kilos pushed into a ring. Half the frog's own weight.
They were nests. Fourteen of them held close to three thousand eggs each, sealed off from the current.
Infrared cameras caught an adult guarding the pool all night, leaving just before dawn.
Then the froglets hatch at under two centimetres. Protected, for a while, by a wall their parent built.

description:
The goliath frog of Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea grows over 34 centimetres long and up to 3.3 kilograms, and a 2019 study found it builds its own nursery ponds.
Along the Mpoula River, researchers found 22 breeding sites where frogs had cleared rock pools or ringed them with stones weighing up to 2 kilograms, more than half their body weight. Fourteen nests held nearly 3,000 eggs each, and time-lapse footage showed an adult guarding a nest all night.
Would you have guessed a frog could build a pond? Comment below.
first_comment: Goliath frog numbers have dropped by more than half in ten years from hunting and logging. Which animal builder should we cover next?
